# Tracking models

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_docs.py from the model cards; do not edit. -->

4 tracking models. Each section says what the model is, whether it may be used commercially and how fast it is; licences and checks are under Details.

Input: a video (its frames in order) and query points `(t, x, y)`. Output: the position of every query in every frame and the probability that it is visible there.

Measured on RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130; `fastforks bench MODEL --size HxW` measures yours. The summary uses one input, 480x854: kernels time with its speed-up over the faster original run, and kernels peak reserved memory with its ratio to the smaller original one. Where measured (one variant per family), a variant's table also lists portable under `torch.compile` and the fp16 TensorRT engine of portable ([export](../export.md); memory: the engine's device memory + torch's peak). – = not measured.

Other devices: [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB](../devices/apple-m1-pro-16gb.md), [NVIDIA L4](../devices/l4-22gb.md), [NVIDIA L40S](../devices/l40s-44gb.md), [NVIDIA A10](../devices/a10-22gb.md), [NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB](../devices/a100-sxm4-40gb.md), [NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000](../devices/rtx-pro-6000-96gb.md); [across devices](../benchmarks.md#other-devices).

| model | commercial | kernels time (ms),<br>speed-up vs original | kernels peak memory (MiB, reserved),<br>ratio to original |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`bootstapir`](#tapir) | yes | 191, 1.3x | 828, 1.1x |

## TAPIR

TAPIR and BootsTAPIR (Google DeepMind, 2023 / 2024): track any point through a whole video offline: a per-frame match from a cost volume, then four temporal refinement passes; BootsTAPIR adds self-training on real videos. Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bootstapir` | synthetic (480x854) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 243<br>240<br>191<br>183<br>fails: ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 4, got 2) | 639 / 774<br>720 / 768<br>769 / 828<br>758 / 832<br>– |
| `tapir` | synthetic (480x854) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 187<br>186<br>138<br>131<br>fails: ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 4, got 2) | 498 / 574<br>630 / 690<br>678 / 750<br>630 / 752<br>– |

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Original code: <https://github.com/google-deepmind/tapnet> at `ceedd60bb9f6`
- Code licence: Apache-2.0 (permissive); files: `LICENSE`
- Weights licence: Apache-2.0
- Licence evidence: <https://github.com/google-deepmind/tapnet/blob/ceedd60bb9f6c9f7c74796e4445aff6c6ddf7c9b/README.md#license-and-disclaimer>
- Training data: Upstream: TAPIR is trained on synthetic Kubric MOVi-E sequences (the panning variant); BootsTAPIR is further trained with BootsTAP self-training on about 15 million unlabelled real video clips (not released). None has a dataset entry here yet.
- Kernel libraries: `fvm_conv`
- Variants: `bootstapir`, `tapir`
- Outputs: tracks, visibility
- Input size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32
- Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): `bootstapir` 3000x4000 (5.6 GiB peak allocated, 6.1 reserved); `tapir` 3000x4000 (5.5 GiB peak allocated, 6.0 reserved)
- `bootstapir` 480x854, first call: portable + torch.compile 207 s (cold Inductor cache).
- `tapir` 480x854, first call: portable + torch.compile 169 s (cold Inductor cache).
- `bootstapir` original 480x854: the authors' mixed-precision option (float16); upstream BootsTAPIR, offline (whole video); frames resized to 256 x 256
- `tapir` original 480x854: the authors' mixed-precision option (float16); upstream TAPIR, offline (whole video); frames resized to 256 x 256
- `bootstapir` load / first call: original 0.6 s / 0.901 s, portable 0.15 s / 0.793 s, kernels 1.19 s / 0.532 s
- `tapir` load / first call: original 0.35 s / 0.827 s, portable 0.16 s / 0.823 s, kernels 0.97 s / 0.515 s
- Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

### Measured

TAP-Vid protocol: frames resized to 256 x 256 (PIL Lanczos) before the model, one query per track at its first visible point, tracked online (TAPNext) or over the whole clip (TAPIR); AJ, delta_avg (< 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 px at 256 x 256) and occlusion accuracy averaged over the videos. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

| variant | dataset | original fp32 | original fp16 | portable | kernels | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bootstapir` | TAP-Vid DAVIS (query first), every 3rd video, AJ / delta_avg / OA % | 65.49 / 76.75 / 92.56 | 65.53 / 76.72 / 92.55 | 65.56 / 76.78 / 92.44 | 65.51 / 76.72 / 92.51 |  |
| `bootstapir` | TAP-Vid DAVIS (query first), AJ / delta_avg / OA % | 62.27 / 74.62 / 89.67 |  | 62.29 / 74.61 / 89.66 | 62.27 / 74.61 / 89.64 |  |
| `tapir` | TAP-Vid DAVIS (query first), every 3rd video, AJ / delta_avg / OA % | 62.63 / 74.54 / 90.14 | 62.62 / 74.60 / 90.18 | 62.74 / 74.59 / 90.11 | 62.73 / 74.55 / 90.21 |  |

Measured on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks 8d5bccf, 2026-11-12 to 2026-11-13.

### Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 3.5e-05 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.0079 and p99 <= 0.028 (absolute error of the output `tracks`).

| variant | kernels error vs original, mean / p99 | GPU, torch | kernels used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bootstapir` | 0.00524 / 0.01845 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `fvm_conv@f1d064e539e1:sm_120` |
| `tapir` | 0.0036 / 0.01425 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `fvm_conv@f1d064e539e1:sm_120` |

### Limitations

- Offline: the whole video is encoded before tracking (features of every frame in memory, about 3 MB per frame); for live video use an online tracker (TAPNext).
- Frames are resized to 256 x 256 (the training size and that of upstream's TAP-Vid numbers), whatever their size and aspect ratio. Upstream's higher-resolution refinement (best at 512 x 512 for BootsTAPIR) is not ported.
- One video per call; all queries of a call share the video.

</details>

## TAPNext

TAPNext (Google DeepMind, 2025): tracks any point through a video, online one frame at a time, as next-token prediction with a ViT + linear-recurrence (RG-LRU) backbone; BootsTAPNext-B and the long-video TAPNext++. Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tapnext` | synthetic (480x854) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 909<br>529<br>382<br>398<br>fails: ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 4, got 2) | 1721 / 1902<br>1220 / 1294<br>1313 / 1374<br>1164 / 1272<br>– |

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Original code: <https://github.com/google-deepmind/tapnet> at `ceedd60bb9f6`
- Code licence: Apache-2.0 (permissive); files: `LICENSE`

- Licence evidence: <https://github.com/google-deepmind/tapnet/blob/ceedd60bb9f6c9f7c74796e4445aff6c6ddf7c9b/README.md#license-and-disclaimer>
- Training data: Upstream: TAPNext is trained on synthetic Kubric MOVi-F sequences and fine-tuned with BootsTAP self-training on unlabelled real videos (not released); TAPNext++ is further fine-tuned on PointOdyssey and Kubric-1024 (1024-frame synthetic sequences). None has a dataset entry here yet.
- Kernel libraries: `fvm_conv`
- Variants: `tapnext`, `tapnext-pp`
- Outputs: tracks, visibility
- Input size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32
- Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): `tapnext` 3000x4000 (4.3 GiB peak allocated, 4.5 reserved); `tapnext-pp` 3000x4000 (4.3 GiB peak allocated, 4.5 reserved)

- `tapnext` load / first call: original 16.92 s / 2.165 s, portable 2.72 s / 0.692 s, kernels 2.63 s / 0.56 s
- Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5
- Speed and memory not measured for: `tapnext-pp`.

### Measured

TAP-Vid protocol: frames resized to 256 x 256 (PIL Lanczos) before the model, one query per track at its first visible point, tracked online (TAPNext) or over the whole clip (TAPIR); AJ, delta_avg (< 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 px at 256 x 256) and occlusion accuracy averaged over the videos. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

| variant | dataset | original fp32 | original fp16 | portable | kernels | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tapnext` | TAP-Vid DAVIS (query first), every 3rd video, AJ / delta_avg / OA % | 71.01 / 82.01 / 95.18 | 71.02 / 82.02 / 95.19 | 71.02 / 82.02 / 95.19 | 71.02 / 82.03 / 95.23 |  |
| `tapnext` | TAP-Vid DAVIS (query first), AJ / delta_avg / OA % | 66.55 / 79.48 / 92.16 | 66.55 / 79.49 / 92.17 | 66.55 / 79.49 / 92.17 | 66.56 / 79.50 / 92.18 |  |

Measured on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, 2026-11-12.

### Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 4.6e-05 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.0063 and p99 <= 0.036 (absolute error of the output `tracks`).

| variant | kernels error vs original, mean / p99 | GPU, torch | kernels used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tapnext` | 0.00369 / 0.02116 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `fvm_conv@f1d064e539e1:sm_120` |
| `tapnext-pp` | 0.00415 / 0.02383 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `fvm_conv@f1d064e539e1:sm_120` |

### Limitations

- Online, causal: a point is tracked from its query frame on; in frames before it the model has no information (the tracks there are its guess, with a low visibility). Query on the first frame, or run the reversed video for the backward part.
- Frames are resized to 256 x 256 (the training size), whatever their size and aspect ratio.
- One video per call; all queries of a call share the video.

</details>
